lines: The crystals told me you were coming. They tell me many things.
Crystalhearth exists outside normal time. Moments layer here — past, present, futures that never were.
The corruption in this place doesn't destroy. It distorts. Reality bends around it like light through a prism.
Be careful what you see in the crystals, Shopkeeper. Some of them remember you.
dialogs.notes: First hint at timeline/rewrite lore. Luxiel knows more than she should.

lines: A crystal formation hums as you approach. Images flicker inside.
A grand hall. Advisors arguing. A man on a throne, face drawn with desperation.
A brilliant artifact — impossibly bright — cracks. The light inverts. The hall shatters.
A woman reaches out. She dissolves.
The vision fades. Your heroes look unsettled. None of them speak.
dialogs.notes: First glimpse of the Grail rupture. No names, just images. Emotional, not expository.

lines: The Oracle showed you something, didn't it?
A king. A broken thing. A choice that unmade the world.
That was not metaphor, Shopkeeper. That happened.
And your Crown — your employer — is the one who broke it.
I intend to fix what he destroyed.
Step aside... or be corrected.
dialogs.notes: Clear apparition, full portrait emerging. First uses title 'The Void Sovereign'. The accusation lands.

lines: Shopkeeper. I need to speak with you. Not as Herald. As... myself.
I've been digging. The King's archives. The sealed records.
The fragments he asked you to find — they're pieces of something called the Grail of Life.
An artifact that can... rewrite history.
The rupture that created the corruption. The reason the void exists.
It was the King's doing. He tried to use the Grail to change the royal succession. It failed.
And everything broke.
I don't know what to believe anymore. But I believe you deserve the truth.
dialogs.notes: Cedric arrives without formal composure. The big reveal. Everything clicks into place.
